newsitem.title: GREECE: NO COVER-UP OF ATHENS BOURSE WOES SAYS SENIOR BANKER.
newsitem.headline: NO COVER-UP OF ATHENS BOURSE WOES SAYS SENIOR BANKER.

text.p: There will be no cover-up of the problems at the Athens Stock Exchange and those responsible will have to pay the cost, the governor of the National Bank of Greece Theodoros Karatzas told financial weekly 'Ekonomikos Tahydromos'.

"A cover-up cures nothing. Should we put cream and talc on a pimple so that it doesn't show? There's no point. The stage that developments have reached means that the pimple has to burst - and everyone has to assume their responsibilities and the consequences of their actions," Karatzas said.

Karatzas said that he hoped that the market had got the message that the National Bank would no longer bail them out after the bank refused to cover the clearing house when Delta Securities defaulted on 2.6 million drachmas in settlements last week.

"The National Bank is not the appropriate vehicle to carry the risk which has been created by other groups or failures," Karatzas said. This may have been the case in the past, he added, but this sort of thinking "has no future". --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
